item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Outlook for iOS and Android: Automatically apply email sensitivity labels from labeled attachments
item.description:
Updated October 7, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why:]

We're introducing support for Microsoft Purview sensitivity label inheritance from attachments in Outlook for iOS and Android. When users attach files that have Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels applied, Outlook can automatically apply or recommend an email sensitivity label based on your organization's configured labeling policies.

This enhancement helps organizations maintain consistent data classification and protection, reduces manual labeling effort for users, and supports compliance objectives across Outlook clients.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Mid-November 2026 (previously late September)

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels.
  • Users of Outlook for iOS and Android.

Platforms/Services

  • Outlook for iOS
  • Outlook for Android
  • Microsoft Purview Information Protection

What will happen

  • When a user attaches one or more files that have sensitivity labels applied, Outlook may automatically apply or recommend an email sensitivity label.
  • The applied or recommended label is determined by your organization's Microsoft Purview sensitivity labeling policies.
  • This behavior helps align email classification with the classification of attached content.
  • Users may experience fewer manual labeling steps when composing messages that contain labeled content.
  • Organizations can benefit from more consistent application of information protection policies across mobile Outlook clients.

[Action Required / Recommendations:]

No admin action is required.

Organizations currently using Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels should:

  • Review existing label publishing policies.
  • Review sensitivity label inheritance and protection configurations.
  • Validate that attachment-based label inheritance aligns with compliance, regulatory, and information protection requirements.
  • Update internal user guidance if your organization provides sensitivity labeling training or documentation.

[Compliance Considerations:]

IssueExplanation
Microsoft Purview sensitivity labelsThis update extends sensitivity label behavior to Outlook for iOS and Android by enabling email labeling based on labeled attachments. Organizations should verify that existing labeling and protection policies produce the desired outcomes for email communications.

For organizations already using Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels, this change helps improve consistency in classification and protection while reducing the risk of emails being sent with a lower sensitivity level than their attachments.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Create interactive slides in PowerPoint with Copilot skill (Windows and Mac)
item.description:
Updated October 7, 2026: We have updated the content and timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why:]

We’re introducing the Copilot skill "Create interactive slide" in PowerPoint for Windows, Mac and web. This capability helps users create interactive, full-slide visuals that explain complex concepts, timelines, comparisons, systems, and data.

  • Users can start creating interactive slides from the PowerPoint ribbon, on the Home and Insert tabs with the "Interactive Slide" button, and in Copilot chat in PowerPoint with the "Create Interactive Slide" skill. 
  • Attendees will be able to interact with slides created by the skill when viewing the slide in PowerPoint Live for Microsoft Teams. 

By making sophisticated visual communication easier to create directly in PowerPoint, this experience can help users communicate ideas more clearly and create engaging presentations with less manual effort.

PowerPoint Live in Microsoft Teams: Each meeting participant can interact independently with slides created using the Create Interactive Slide skill. Interactions are not shared; attendees will see their own interactions, but not the presenter’s or other attendees’ interactions. Support for synchronizing presenter interactions across the meeting is planned as a future improvement.

[Rollout schedule:]

Frontier and Microsoft 365 Insider Beta channel 

  • Skill now available in PowerPoint for Windows, Mac and web.
  • Ribbon Button in PowerPoint for Windows and Mac: By late September 2026 
  • Skill and Ribbon Button in PowerPoint for the web: By early October 2026

Current channel (Preview)

  • Skill and Ribbon Button in PowerPoint for Windows and Mac: By early October 2026

Worldwide

  • Skill and ribbon button in PowerPoint for Windows, Mac and web: rollout will start in mid-October 2026 and is expected to complete by end of October 2026.
  • Attendee interaction now available in PowerPoint Live in Microsoft Teams.

[Impact on your organization:]

Who is affected:

  • PowerPoint for Windows, Mac and web users who have access to this capability.

Platforms:

  • PowerPoint for Windows, Mac and web.
  • Interactive slides are interactive in PowerPoint for iPad and will appear as non-interactive images in PowerPoint for iPhone and Android.

After the feature becomes available, eligible users will be able to use the Create interactive slide skill to produce or update full-slide visual experiences for scenarios such as:

  • Explaining complex concepts.
  • Presenting timelines.
  • Comparing options or information.
  • Illustrating systems and relationships.
  • Communicating data visually.

Organizations participating in the Microsoft Copilot Frontier program can evaluate the preview experience before general availability. Frontier capabilities are pre-release experiences and may change before reaching general availability.

[Action required / recommendations:]

No action is required before rollout. There are no admin settings for this capability.

A Copilot license is required.

We recommend that administrators:

  • Review this information with presentation support, adoption, training, and help desk teams.
  • Consider identifying Frontier participants who can evaluate the capability and provide feedback before general availability.
  • Update internal PowerPoint guidance or training materials if your organization maintains standardized presentation-creation processes.
  • Review the Microsoft Copilot Frontier program documentation: Get started with the Microsoft Copilot Frontier Program.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Call quality feedback surveys for Teams Rooms on Android
item.description:

To help improve meeting experiences and provide organizations with insights into call quality, Microsoft Teams is introducing call quality feedback (CQF) surveys for Microsoft Teams Rooms on Android. These surveys allow users to rate the quality of calls and meetings and provide feedback about audio, video, and screen-sharing experiences. Customer feedback collected through these surveys helps Microsoft improve Teams meeting quality and reliability across devices and services.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 543713.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in November 2026

[Impact on your organization]

  • Organizations using Microsoft Teams Rooms on Android devices.
  • Users who participate in meetings on Teams Rooms on Android devices.

Platforms/Services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Microsoft Teams Rooms on Android
  • Teams admin center (for device app updates)

What will happen

  • Users will periodically see a call quality feedback survey after meetings end on Teams Rooms on Android devices.
  • Users can provide feedback on call quality, video quality, audio quality, and screen-sharing experiences.
  • Feedback will be used by Microsoft to improve Teams products and services.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Edge: Retiring legacy sign-in implementation on Windows
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Microsoft Edge is retiring its legacy direct-WAM sign-in implementation on Windows starting with Microsoft Edge version 157, completing the consolidation onto the OneAuth authentication library.

This change standardizes authentication flows across Microsoft 365 client applications, simplifies platform supportability, eliminates dual-stack authentication code paths, and provides improved diagnostic and recovery mechanisms. Windows Web Account Manager (WAM) itself is not being deprecated; OneAuth continues to use Windows WAM.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): Rollout begins in early November 2026 and is expected to complete in early November 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Organizations using Microsoft Edge on Windows.
  • Users with Edge profiles that have not yet automatically migrated to OneAuth.
  • Organizations that explicitly disabled OneAuth WAM using --disable-features=msOneAuthWAM.

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft Edge on Windows
  • Browser sign-in, identity, token fetch, Single Sign-On, and account synchronization experiences

What will happen:

  • Starting with Microsoft Edge version 157, all remaining profiles will transition directly to OneAuth authentication.
  • The fallback legacy WAM path will default off under all circumstances.
  • Most users will transition transparently.
  • In rare cases, users may need to sign in to Microsoft Edge again.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

We recommend that admins identify unmigrated profiles and test the transition before Microsoft Edge version 157 reaches their environment.

  • Navigate to edge://signin-internals in Microsoft Edge.
  • Under Edge Auth Library Information > Library, confirm whether the profile shows OneAuth or WAM.
  • If OneAuth is displayed, the profile is already using the modern path and no action is required.
  • If WAM is displayed, the profile is still using the legacy path.

On pilot test devices running Microsoft Edge version 155 or later, admins can test the transition before version 157 by launching Edge with this force flag:

msedge.exe --enable-features=msForceOneAuthWAM

Verify that edge://signin-internals reflects OneAuth, and confirm that browser sign-in, Single Sign-On, and account synchronization work as expected.

Inform support teams that a small number of users might see a sign-in action on the profile menu after updating to Edge version 157. If users experience sign-in issues, collect OneAuth logs with:

msedge.exe --enable-features=msForceOneAuthWAM --enable-logging -v=1 --oneauth-log-level=5

Default log location: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\chrome_debug.log

[Compliance considerations:]

Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Admins can validate and manage the transition through Microsoft Edge configuration and feature flags. Review your Microsoft Edge deployment and policy management practices for group-based rollout controls.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Analytics for desk utilization in Teams Pro Management portal
item.description:
[What and Why:]

We’re expanding analytics in the Microsoft Teams Pro Management portal to include utilization insights for bookable desks. IT admins will be able to better understand how desk spaces are being used across their organization, with insights into desk utilization, reservations, occupancy, and peak usage patterns. Desk-specific filters, including location and desk mode, will help admins analyze usage across their workplace and make more informed space planning decisions.

For utilization analytics to be enabled, a desk needs to have one or more peripheral device associated, and the desk needs to be licensed with Microsoft Teams Shared Space license or Microsoft Teams Shared Space - Single Space license.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 570648


[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on early November 2026 and expect to complete by mid December 2026.


[Impact on Your Organization:]

These insights can help organizations better understand how bookable desks are being used and inform workplace and space planning decisions.


[Action Required/Recommendations:]

To enable utilization analytics, a desk must have one or more associated peripheral devices and be licensed with a Microsoft Teams Shared Space or Microsoft Teams Shared Space - Single Space license.


[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] 'Record A Skill' Capability in PowerPoint Copilot
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Microsoft is introducing a Record a Skill capability in Copilot for PowerPoint. This capability helps users create reusable skills by recording actions in PowerPoint, so they can more easily repeat common PowerPoint tasks with Copilot.

Instead of manually recreating the same steps each time, users can record a workflow and use it as a repeatable skill. This can help users save time, improve consistency, and make Copilot in PowerPoint more useful for recurring presentation tasks.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins in early October 2026 and is expected to complete in early October 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Users who use Copilot in PowerPoint and create or reuse skills for PowerPoint workflows.

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft PowerPoint
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot

What will happen:

  • Users will be able to record actions in PowerPoint to create a repeatable skill for use with Copilot in PowerPoint.
  • Recorded skills can help users repeat common PowerPoint workflows more efficiently.
  • The capability is part of the existing skills experience with Copilot in PowerPoint.
  • The feature will become available automatically as it rolls out.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required.

You may want to:

  • Inform helpdesk and training teams about the new Record a Skill capability in Copilot for PowerPoint.
  • Share guidance with users who frequently repeat the same PowerPoint tasks and may benefit from creating reusable skills.
  • Review the support article when it becomes available: https://aka.ms/ppt-record-a-skill.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft 365: Targeted Release retirement
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Targeted release for Microsoft 365 services will be retiring in January 2027 as Microsoft 365 transitions to three release options: Frontier, Standard release, and Deferred release.

To prepare for this change, review users currently enrolled in Targeted release and configure the release preference that best meets your organization's needs.

Choose your preferred release preference in the Microsoft 365 admin center:

  • Preview access
    • Frontier: Opt in to preview eligible AI and non-AI features before general availability.
  • General availability access
    • Standard release: Receive updates at general availability.
    • Deferred release: Receive eligible major updates approximately 30 days after Standard release begins, allowing additional time for validation and readiness activities.

In November 2026, administrators will no longer be able to add users to, remove users from, or modify Targeted release enrollments. Additional information about the related admin experience changes will be shared in a future Message center post.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Now: Review current release preferences and enroll users in Frontier, Standard release, or Deferred release if needed.
  • November 2026: Targeted release enrollment changes are disabled.
  • November 2026: Unified release preferences experience becomes available. Update your release preferences (Frontier, Standard release, Deferred release) in the unified release preferences experience.
  • January 2027: Targeted release retires. Targeted release assignments are no longer used for Microsoft 365 feature delivery.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Organizations with users or tenants enrolled in Microsoft 365 Targeted release.
  • Administrators who manage Microsoft 365 release preferences.

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Microsoft Teams
  • Outlook (New)
  • Outlook on the web
  • Office for the Web
  • Microsoft OneDrive
  • SharePoint Online
  • Some components of Exchange Online

What will happen:

  • In November 2026, administrators can no longer add, remove, or modify Targeted release assignments. 
  • In November 2026, administrators can configure Frontier, Standard release, and Deferred release preferences from a single unified release preferences experience in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Users currently assigned to Targeted release will continue receiving eligible Microsoft 365 features through existing Targeted release assignments until Targeted release is retired.
  • Targeted Release retires in January 2027, and Targeted release will no longer used for Microsoft 365 feature delivery.
  • After retirement, feature rollout timing follows your configured Frontier, Standard release, or Deferred release preference.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

Before November 2026, administrators should complete the following actions:

  • Identify and update users currently assigned to Targeted release before enrollment changes are disabled. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Settings > Org settings > Organization profile > Release preferences.
  • Evaluate and select the appropriate Standard release or Deferred release preference for your organization under Copilot > Settings > View all > Copilot Release preferences: General availability.
  • Evaluate Frontier and, where appropriate, enroll eligible users who require early access to preview experiences under Copilot > Settings > View all > Copilot Frontier.
  • Review the Learn documentation on Targeted release retirement for detailed transition guidance.
  • Notify change management teams, support teams, security and compliance teams, pilot groups, and key IT stakeholders about the upcoming retirement and required transition actions.

In November 2026, release preferences for Frontier, Standard release, and Deferred release can be managed through the unified release preferences experience in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Also, the current experience for managing Standard release and Deferred release preferences will be retired when the unified release preferences experience becomes available. Additional details about related admin experience changes will be shared in a future Message center post.

[Additional Resources:]

  • Configure new Standard and Deferred release options for Microsoft 365
  • Plan for the Retirement of Targeted Release in Microsoft 365

[Compliance considerations:]

  • Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership? Administrators will manage release preferences through the Microsoft 365 admin center and should evaluate user/group assignment needs for Frontier, Standard release, and Deferred release.
  • Does the change alter how admins can monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities? Organizations should update internal release-management and readiness processes because Targeted release assignments will no longer be used after retirement.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft 365: The Next Generation of File & Folder Sharing
item.description:
Updated October 7, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why:]

We're introducing the third-generation Microsoft 365 sharing experience to make collaboration simpler, smarter, and more secure by default. At the center of this update is a new hero link—a single sharing link that controls access to a file or folder.

Users will see one consistent sharing experience whether they copy a link, share through email, or use the browser URL. The hero link consolidates sharing controls into a single link that can be updated after it has been shared, reducing the need to create and resend new links when access requirements change.

[Rollout schedule:]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Rolling out early October 2026 (previously mid-September) through end of November 2026 (previously late October)

[Impact on your organization:]

Who is affected: All users who share or manage files and folders in Microsoft 365.

Platforms and services: SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft 365 file-sharing experiences.

What will happen:

  • Every file and folder will have a single primary sharing link, called the hero link, displayed in the sharing dialog.
  • The hero link settings determine who can access the item beyond people who are explicitly granted access.
  • Adding people directly to a file or folder remains unchanged and continues to be the simplest way to share content.

Screenshot - Add people screen when sharing 

  • By default, the hero link is set to Only people added to the file, meaning the link itself does not grant access to anyone.

Screenshot - Share file view with hero link

  • Users can broaden access to people in the organization with the link or, where permitted by organizational policy, to anyone with the link.
  • Users can choose whether recipients can view, edit, or view without downloading, depending on available permissions.
  • Changing the audience for the hero link updates the existing link rather than creating a new one.
  • If recipients cannot open a previously shared file, the sender can expand access on the same hero link without redistributing a new URL.
  • Existing sharing links will continue to function and will appear under Other links in the sharing dialog.
  • Effective access remains the most permissive combination of direct permissions, inherited permissions, group-based permissions, and link-based permissions.
  • Users will see a tutorial experience upon opening the new share dialog for the first time.

[Action required/Recommendations:]

No action is required before rollout.

Organizations should consider the following preparation activities:

  • Review internal sharing guidance and end-user documentation to reflect the new single-link sharing model.
  • Communicate the updated sharing experience to users who regularly collaborate across teams and organizations.
  • Evaluate site-level default sharing settings where different sharing behaviors are required.

Learn more:

  • Walkthrough Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3RpE0KrQmcA&t=4s
  • Announcement Blog: https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/onedriveblog/simple-smart-and-secure-the-next-step-in-sharing-files-in-microsoft-365/4411655

Admin controls

  • Administrators can configure the default audience for the hero link at the SharePoint site collection or OneDrive level by using the DefaultMainLinkScope parameter in SharePoint PowerShell.
  • Supported values are:
    • OnlyPeopleAdded (default)
    • Organization
  • There is currently no tenant-wide equivalent setting for the hero link audience.
  • DefaultMainLinkScope controls only the default audience and does not prevent users from broadening access when allowed by policy.
  • Hero links start with view permissions by default.
  • Existing default sharing link settings and link expiration policies continue to apply to legacy links and do not govern hero links.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Entra: Authenticated password change in My Sign-Ins
item.description:
Updated October 7, 2026: We have updated the timeline and content. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why]

We're introducing a new Microsoft Entra capability that allows authenticated password changes directly from My Sign-Ins using an existing strong credential, such as a passkey, FIDO2 security key, or Windows Hello for Business. Users can complete this action even if they don't know their current password and without using self-service password reset (SSPR) or contacting the helpdesk.

Many organizations are adopting authenticated password change but still maintain passwords for legacy applications and services. This update helps reduce password-related support requests and removes a common barrier to adoption. The feature is disabled by default and requires administrator enablement before users can access it.

[Rollout Schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide and GCC): Beginning in mid-October 2026 and expected to complete by late October 2026

[Impact on Your Organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Entra administrators who manage password change settings
  • Users who have a registered authenticated password change method (passkey, FIDO2 security key, or Windows Hello for Business) and also maintain a password
  • Organizations that choose to enable the feature

Platforms/Services

  • Microsoft Entra
  • My Sign-Ins (mysignins.microsoft.com)

What will happen

  • Because this feature is off by default, there is no change to your users' experience unless you turn it on. 
  • After the feature is enabled, eligible users will see a new Change password option in My Sign-Ins.
  • Users can authenticate set a new password without knowing their existing password.
  • Users are not required to enroll in or use SSPR to complete this action.
  • Administrators can choose to enable or disable the capability through Microsoft Entra management interfaces available at release.
  • Authentication continues to require a strong password change method, such as a passkey, FIDO2 security key, or Windows Hello for Business.
  • The setting is tenant-wide: you can turn it on for your entire tenant or leave it off for everyone. There is no per-user or per-group scoping. 

[Action Required/Recommendations]

No action is required.

If your organization plans to support authenticated password change:

  • Review your password management and authenticated password change strategy.
  • Evaluate whether enabling this capability aligns with your organization's security and support requirements.
  • Communicate the new self-service capability to helpdesk and support teams.
  • Update internal user guidance and documentation as needed.
  • If your organization chooses to offer authenticated password changes, enable the feature through the Microsoft Entra admin experience or supported APIs when it becomes available in October 2026.

Learn more 

  • Microsoft Learn documentation will be available when the feature releases in October. 

[Compliance Considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. The feature is disabled by default and requires explicit administrator enablement.
Does the change modify how users can access or correct their personal data?Yes. Users gain a new self-service method to update their password using an existing authenticated password change.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Default visibility of additional profile card properties in Microsoft 365 profile cards
item.description:
Updated October 7, 2026: We have decided not to move forward with this change at this time. We apologize for any inconvenience.

[What and Why:]

To help people discover and understand organizational information more easily, Microsoft is changing the default visibility of 11 existing profile card properties in Microsoft 365 profile cards. Today, these properties can be populated from Microsoft Entra ID and other supported external data sources such as People Graph Connectors and Microsoft 365 Organizational Data, but they are disabled by default and require administrators to manually enable them. You can find more on the existing profile card property management here.

With this update, these properties will be displayed by default when populated with data. This helps organizations surface relevant employee information more consistently while reducing administrative effort for commonly used profile attributes. Organizations retain administrative controls to manage visibility according to their business, privacy, and compliance requirements.

The following properties are included in this update:

  1. Division
  2. Role
  3. Employee number
  4. Employee type
  5. Cost center
  6. User principal name (UPN)
  7. Alias
  8. Fax
  9. Street address
  10. State
  11. Postal code

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We have decided not to move forward with this change at this time.

[Impact to your organization:]

Who is affected 

  1. Global Administrators and People Administrators responsible for profile card management.
  2. Organizations with users whose profile data includes one or more of the affected properties.

Platforms/Services 

  1. Microsoft 365 Profile Cards
  2. Microsoft Entra ID
  3. Microsoft 365 Organizational Data
  4. Microsoft Entra People Graph Connectors
  5. Microsoft Graph profile card management APIs
  6. Microsoft 365 admin center

What will happen 

  1. The 11 listed properties will automatically appear on profile cards when the corresponding attributes contain data.
  2. The change is enabled by default.
  3. Attributes sourced from Microsoft Entra ID, Microsoft 365 Organizational Data, and Microsoft Entra People Graph Connectors follow the same visibility behavior.
  4. No changes are made to underlying attribute values or source systems.
  5. No changes are required from end users.
  6. Tenants that have never configured profile card settings will automatically receive the new default visibility behavior.
  7. Only properties with populated values will appear on profile cards.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

If your organization does not want specific properties displayed on profile cards, action is recommended before October 31, 2026.

Review current profile card configuration 

Use Microsoft Graph to review existing profile card property settings:

HTTP

GET  https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/admin/people/profileCardProperties 

Hide properties before rollout 
To prevent a property from being displayed, configure the property as hidden using Microsoft Graph.
Example: Hide Employee Number
HTTP 

POST
https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/admin/people/profileCardProperties 
Content-Type: application/json 
{ 
"directoryPropertyName": "EmployeeId", 
 "isVisible": false  
}

For each property, you can use the property mappings below:

Profile card label directoryPropertyName 
DivisionDivision
RoleRole
Employee numberEmployeeId
Employee typeEmployeeType
Cost centerCostCenter
User principal name (UPN)UserPrincipalName
AliasAlias
FaxFax
Street addressStreetAddress
StateStateOrProvince
Postal codePostalCode

Important: Each property requires a separate Microsoft Graph API call. Bulk enable or bulk disable operations are not currently supported. You can find more on using Microsoft Graph APIs for showing and hiding profile card attributes here. Recommended Administrator Actions

  1. Verify your current profile card configuration using Microsoft Graph and review which of the affected properties contain data in your tenant.
  2. Use Microsoft Graph Profile Card APIs to hide any properties that should remain unavailable to users before rollout begins on October 31, 2026.
  3. Communicate the upcoming change to help desk and support teams.

After rollout, administrators can continue managing profile card visibility through Microsoft 365 admin center > People settings > Profile cards. Changes made can take up to 24 hours to be reflected on profile cards across Microsoft 365 experiences.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft 365 Copilot: Legal agent available in Frontier worldwide
item.description:
Updated October 7, 2026: We have updated the timeline and content. GA release will now be tracked separately in an upcoming MC post. Thank you for your patience.  

[What and Why]

Microsoft is expanding the availability of Copilot for Legal in Microsoft 365 Copilot in Word to Frontier users worldwide in Public Preview.

Copilot for Legal was previously released in Frontier preview for users located in the United States only. This update expands access globally, enabling more organizations to benefit from this capability.

Copilot for Legal is a vertical-specific Microsoft 365 Copilot experience designed for legal professionals, built directly into Word. It helps legal teams review and negotiate contracts by identifying risks, comparing clauses to internal playbooks, and proposing edits using Word’s native tracked changes.

This update helps reduce manual review time while keeping legal professionals fully in control of document workflows.

[Rollout Schedule]

  • Frontier Preview: Available starting in mid-June 2026.
  • General Availability: GA release will now be tracked separately in an upcoming MC post.

[Impact on Your Organization] 

Who is affected

  • Organizations enrolled in the Microsoft 365 Copilot Frontier program
  • Users with Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, particularly legal professionals (for example, in-house counsel, contract managers, legal ops)

Organizations not enrolled in the Frontier program are not impacted.

Platforms/Services

  • Microsoft Word (Copilot) – desktop
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot (Frontier)

What will happen

  • Copilot for Legal will be available in Copilot Chat in Word via the “+” (plus) menu.
  • Users can:
    • Review contracts to identify risks and non-standard clauses
    • Generate redlines using Word tracked changes
    • Compare clauses against internal legal playbooks
    • Analyze document sections for compliance with internal standards
    • Receive responses grounded in document content with citations
  • The feature is enabled by default for tenants enrolled in Frontier.
  • No separate installation is required.
  • The feature is available immediately after users update to a supported version of Word.
  • Availability depends on:
    • Frontier program enrollment
    • Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing
  • There is no dedicated admin or user toggle to disable this feature
  • Access is controlled through Frontier enrollment and Copilot license assignment.

[Action Required / Recommendations]

No action is required if you do not plan to use this feature.

If you plan to use this feature:

  • Enroll your tenant in the Frontier Public Preview program.
  • Ensure Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses are assigned to eligible users.
  • Review internal legal workflows that may benefit from:
    • Contract analysis
    • Playbook-based reviews
    • AI-assisted redlining
  • Communicate this capability to legal teams.
  • Update internal documentation or helpdesk guidance if applicable.

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed (such as documents, emails, chats, etc.)? If so, how and to what extent?Yes. Copilot for Legal processes existing document content in Word to analyze contracts, compare clauses to internal playbooks, and generate suggested edits.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data? If so, summarize the changes.Yes. The change introduces Copilot for Legal within Microsoft 365 Copilot that uses AI to interact with and analyze customer document data.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Improved file sharing experience in external chats
item.description:
Updated October 6, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

We’re improving the file-sharing experience in Microsoft Teams external (federated) chats by making the Attach file (paperclip) and drag-and-drop experiences available by default. This change only impacts tenants who have not adjusted the policy that controls file attachment in an external Teams chat. To opt out of this change, disable the capability using the Teams PowerShell setting provided in the “Action required and recommendations” section below. This can be done before the rollout and your policy setting will be respected. This update does not change your OneDrive or SharePoint external-sharing settings or override existing access restrictions. 

Prior to this change, when existing OneDrive and SharePoint policies allow, users can already share files in external chats by sharing a link to the file. This update makes that flow easier by adding the Attach file (paperclip) and drag-and-drop experiences directly in Teams. Files uploaded from the user’s device are stored in the sender’s OneDrive, while cloud files remain stored in their existing location. Teams then assigns permissions to chat participants, subject to existing OneDrive and SharePoint sharing policies. Senders can still review, modify, or remove file access before sending the message. This reduces the need to assign permissions manually, while allowing senders to stay in control.

  • More info: Share files and Loop in external chats - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

[Rollout schedule]

  • Targeted Release: Beginning in late October 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026
  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning in late October 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Teams external access (federation)
  • This change applies only to organizations where the setting has not been explicitly configured. Any customers who have left the configuration in the default state will be impacted. 
  • Users participating in external 1:1 chats, external group chats, and meeting chats

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • External (federated) 1:1 chats
  • External (federated) group chats
  • Meeting chats
  • Teams desktop app
  • Teams web app

What will happen

  • The ability for users to attach and share files in external chats will be enabled for all Microsoft 365 tenants, unless your organization has previously explicitly disabled this setting in Teams. Any customers who have left the configuration in the default state will be impacted.
  • Users can already paste file links into external chants. This ability is unchanged. With this change, users will also have the ability to attach and share files using the paperclip option or drag and drop in external (federated) chats.
  • Files shared through these experiences continue to be stored and shared through OneDrive or SharePoint. Files uploaded from a user’s device are stored in the sender’s OneDrive, while existing cloud files remain in their current location. 
  • When automatic permission assignment is enabled, Teams assigns permissions to participants in the external chat for files uploaded using paperclip or drag-and-drop, subject to existing OneDrive and SharePoint policies.
  • Senders can review, modify, or remove sharing permissions before sending a file.
  • Senders can continue to modify or revoke access after a file has been shared.
  • Automatic permission assignment applies only to files shared through the paperclip or drag-and-drop experience.
  • The files will be shared as hyperlinks after send. 
  • Existing OneDrive and SharePoint sharing controls continue to govern access.
  • Existing sensitivity labels, domain restrictions, and security protections continue to apply.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required to preserve external-sharing restrictions already configured in OneDrive and SharePoint; this update does not change those restrictions. To review or change these controls, see Manage sharing settings for SharePoint and OneDrive in Microsoft 365. 

[To disable file attachments in external chats]

To opt out of this change, apply the following Teams PowerShell setting if you have not already explicitly configured this setting:

Set-CsTeamsFilesPolicy -Identity Global -FileSharingInChatsWithExternalUsers Disabled

Verify the setting:

Get-CsTeamsFilesPolicy | Select Identity, FileSharingInChatsWithExternalUsers

Recommended actions:

  • Review your SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft Entra external sharing configuration because these settings continue to govern what external recipients can access.
  • Inform helpdesk and support teams about the updated attachment experience and the distinction between Teams attachment controls and OneDrive/SharePoint access controls. 
  • Update user training and internal documentation as needed.
  • Communicate to users that:
    • They can attach files directly in chats with people outside the organization.
    • When automatic permission assignment is enabled, Teams assigns chat participants access to files shared via paperclip icon, subject to existing OneDrive and SharePoint policies. Senders can review, modify, or remove access before sending.
    • Pasted file links retain their existing permissions.
    • Files uploaded to external chats are stored in the sender's OneDrive and display.

Optional configuration to allow attachments without automatic permission assignment:

To disable automatic permission assignment while continuing to allow file attachments in external chats:

Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy -Identity Global -AutoShareFilesInExternalChats Disabled

If automatic permission assignment is disabled, users may need to manually grant access to shared files before external recipients can open them.

Allow several hours for policy changes to propagate before users see the updated experience.

Learn more:

  • Share files and Loop in external chats - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Uploaded files shared through Attach or drag-and-drop can automatically receive permissions for participants in external chats. Existing OneDrive and SharePoint controls continue to govern access. Uploaded files are stored in the sender’s OneDrive.
Does the change provide a new way of communicating between users, tenants, or subscriptions?Yes. The direct file-attachment experience in external (federated) chats becomes available by default; the existing ability to paste file links remains unchanged.
Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. Admins can separately control Teams file attachments and automatic permission assignment through Teams PowerShell policies. OneDrive and SharePoint sharing settings continue to govern external file access.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft OneDrive and SharePoint: Generate smart tables of contents for PDFs on the web with Copilot
item.description:
[What and Why:]

We are introducing Smart Table of Contents (Smart TOC) in the Microsoft OneDrive and SharePoint PDF viewer on the web for users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. When a PDF does not already contain a table of contents, users can ask Copilot to generate a hierarchical, clickable structure that makes it easier to navigate long documents and move between sections. This feature is available only on the web in the initial release and is generated only when a user explicitly requests it.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Targeted Release (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in early December 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-December 2026.
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in mid-December 2026 and is expected to complete by late December 2026.
  • General Availability (GCC): Rollout will begin in mid-December 2026 and is expected to complete by late December 2026.
  • General Availability (GCC High): Rollout will begin in mid-December 2026 and is expected to complete by late December 2026.
  • General Availability (DoD): Rollout will begin in mid-December 2026 and is expected to complete by late December 2026.

This is a gradual rollout, and not all eligible users will receive the feature at the same time.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

  • Who is affected: Users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license who access PDF files in OneDrive and SharePoint on the web.
  • Platforms/Services: OneDrive, SharePoint, Microsoft 365 Copilot, PDF viewer on the web.

What will happen:

  • The Smart TOC entry point will appear when an eligible user opens a PDF that does not already contain table-of-contents information.
  • The feature is available only in the OneDrive and SharePoint PDF viewer on the web during the initial release.
  • Mobile and desktop applications are not included at this time.
  • Copilot analyzes document structure and generates nested, clickable entries mapped to pages or page ranges.
  • Users with edit permissions can save the generated table of contents into the PDF.
  • The saved table of contents can be displayed by compatible PDF editors.
  • Users with view-only permissions can generate and use Smart TOC for navigation but cannot save the generated table of contents.
  • Smart TOC is available only to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
  • AI-generated content may be inaccurate, particularly for scanned or OCR-based PDF files.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No immediate admin action is required.

Before rollout, you may want to:

  • Review Microsoft 365 Copilot license assignments for users who should have access to this capability.
  • Inform eligible users, helpdesk personnel, and support teams about the new PDF navigation experience.
  • Update internal documentation to clarify that saving a generated table of contents requires edit permissions on the PDF.
  • Encourage users to validate AI-generated table-of-contents entries when accuracy is important.

[Compliance considerations:]

  • Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed? Yes. Copilot processes PDF content that the licensed user is already authorized to access in order to generate a table of contents for navigation. Existing file permissions are respected, and saving changes requires edit permissions.
  • Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data? Yes. Copilot analyzes PDF document structure and generates an AI-created hierarchical table of contents. The experience is user-initiated and does not run automatically.
  • Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI? Yes. Eligible users can request Copilot to generate a table of contents for PDF files that do not already contain one.
  • Does the change allow a user to enable and disable the feature themselves? Yes. The feature is user-initiated and only runs when a licensed user chooses to generate a Smart TOC.

The experience will clearly indicate that the table of contents was AI generated and may contain inaccuracies.

item.description:

[What and why]

We are improving the OneDrive sync experience on Windows desktop to provide clearer, more actionable guidance when file and folder paths exceed the supported 520-character limit. The updated experience will show exactly how many characters a path exceeds the limit and will provide a guided flow to rename or move affected items so they can sync successfully.

This improvement addresses a common OneDrive sync issue by reducing user confusion, minimizing workflow disruption, and helping users resolve errors faster.

This update is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 557563.

[Rollout schedule]

  • All users of the OneDrive sync client on Windows desktop

Platforms and services

  • OneDrive for Business (Windows desktop sync client)

What will happen

Max path errors are one of the most commonly reported issues by OneDrive sync users. Currently, when a file or folder path exceeds the 520-character sync limit, the error message only states how many characters the path exceeds the limit and asks users to shorten it. In addition, File Explorer limitations may prevent users from renaming paths over 260 characters, and the sync client may stop syncing until the issue is resolved.

As part of this improved error experience, when users encounter max path errors, the sync client will continue running and users will be guided through a custom rename and move experience.

With this update:

  • The sync client will continue running when users encounter max path errors
  • Users will be guided through a custom rename and move experience to resolve issues directly

The rename experience will:

  • Show the number of over-limit characters
  • Highlight which items in the path can be renamed
  • Allow renames even when the path exceeds 260 characters

Screenshot - Custom rename dialog

The move experience will:

  • Show over-limit character counts in a guided interface
  • Display warning dialogs for over-limit shared items in OneDrive
  • Display warning dialogs for over-limit items in shortcuts

Screenshot - Example warning dialog for overlimit items in shortcuts

These enhancements are designed to reduce troubleshooting time and improve the overall sync experience.

[Action required and recommendations]

item.title: [planForChange] Private tasks now stored in your private plan in Planner
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Microsoft is updating how private tasks are stored in Microsoft Planner. Beginning in November 2026, private tasks created in Planner and Planner-powered experiences will be stored in a user's own private Planner plan instead of the Microsoft To Do task store.

This enables richer Planner capabilities, such as labels and task history, while maintaining the same private experience. Private tasks remain visible only to the task owner and cannot be shared or assigned to others. This change aligns private task management with the Planner platform while preserving enterprise compliance and security protections.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins in early November 2026.
  • Expected completion: late November 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Users who create and manage private tasks in Planner and Planner-powered experiences.

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft Planner
  • Planner on the web
  • Planner-powered experiences
  • Microsoft To Do

What will happen:

  • New private tasks will be stored in a private Planner plan.
  • Users will continue to see existing private tasks in Planner My Tasks.
  • Private tasks remain private to the task owner.
  • Private tasks cannot be shared or assigned to others.
  • Additional Planner task capabilities, such as labels, will become available.
  • New private tasks created in Planner will no longer appear in Microsoft To Do.
  • Existing compliance and security protections continue to apply.
  • The feature is enabled automatically.
  • No administrator action is required for deployment.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No action is required.

You may want to:

  • Inform support and help desk teams of the change.
  • Review any internal documentation that references Planner private tasks appearing in Microsoft To Do.
  • Review the Microsoft Planner service description and admin documentation.
  • Communicate the updated experience to affected users.

[Compliance considerations:]

Does the change store new customer data, if so, where, and is the data cached or permanently stored?Yes. New private tasks will be stored in a user's private Planner plan instead of the Microsoft To Do task store.
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Private task storage changes from Microsoft To Do to Planner for new private tasks. Existing private tasks remain visible in Planner My Tasks.
Does the change modify retention policies, holds, or deletion workflows?Yes. Organizations should validate any retention, discovery, reporting, or governance processes that depend on Microsoft To Do storage.
Does the change alter how admins can monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities?Yes. Admins may need to account for the storage change from To Do to Planner in reporting or governance processes.
Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI?No. This is a Planner task storage and experience update, not a generative AI capability.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Migrate Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing before EWS deprecation
item.description:
Updated October 5, 2026: Gov rollout of this feature is paused at this time. We will communicate via Message center when we are ready to proceed. We apologize for any inconvenience.

[What and Why:]

Exchange Web Services (EWS) deprecation begins October 1, 2026. Cross-tenant collaboration features — Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing — currently rely on EWS.

Cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips will be available by September 2026 and Calendar Sharing will be available by mid-October 2026 via Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy, which replaces EWS-based cross-tenant collaboration.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Worldwide: We will begin rolling out in August 2026 and expect to complete by September 15, 2026 for Free/Busy, Mailtips and October 15, 2026 for Calendar Sharing.
  • GCC, GCC High, DoD: We will communicate via Message center when we are ready to proceed.

[Impact on your organization:]

Sharing Free/Busy, Calendars, and MailTips (e.g., out of office message) with another Microsoft 365 organization via Organization Relationship or Sharing Policy relies on Exchange Web Services (EWS), which is being deprecated. To preserve these cross-tenant collaboration scenarios, you will need to start migrating to Microsoft 365 Cross Tenant Access Policy.

Your tenant is affected if it uses any of the following Exchange Online configurations:

  • Organization Relationships — sharing Free/Busy or MailTips with other Microsoft 365 tenants 
  • Sharing Policies — sharing calendars externally, either via invitations sent to recipients in other Microsoft 365 organizations or calendars published for anonymous access via an internet URL

Run these commands in Exchange Online PowerShell to check if your tenant is affected: 

    • Get-OrganizationRelationship | Format-List Name, DomainNames, Enabled, FreeBusyAccessEnabled, FreeBusyAccessLevel, FreeBusyAccessScope, MailTipsAccessEnabled, MailTipsAccessLevel, MailTipsAccessScopeIf results show (1) Enabled: True, and (2) either FreeBusyAccessEnabled: True or MailtipsAccessEnabled: True, and (3) the external organization is hosted in Microsoft 365, your tenant is affected and in scope to migrate. Else, no action is needed. 
    • Get-SharingPolicy | Format-List Name, Domains, Enabled, DefaultIf results show (1) Enabled: True, and (2) the Domains property contains at least one rule with a CalendarSharingFreeBusy access level (Simple, Detail, or Reviewer), and (3) the targeted external organization is hosted in Microsoft 365, and (4) the policy is assigned to one or more mailboxes, your tenant is affected and in scope to migrate. Else, no action is needed.
    • Note: rules that begin with Anonymous: represent calendar publishing to anonymous internet recipients via a published URL - these also appear in this output.

What happens if I do nothing:

Starting October 1, 2026, Exchange Web Services (EWS) will be gradually disabled in line with previous communications linked to this message. As this rollout reaches your tenant, cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing that rely on EWS will be affected — recipients in partner organizations may no longer see Free/Busy, MailTips, or shared calendars from your tenant. 

If your organization is not ready to migrate, you can retain EWS access by following the guidance of the latest blog we published: ExchangeOnline EWS, Your Time is Almost Up (EWSEnabled set to True) while you prepare and execute the migration steps attached to this message. EWS access through this extension will remain available until the final EWS shutdown on April 1, 2027. 

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

  • Follow this Message center post for updates to the rollout schedule. To avoid impact, plan to migrate after the rollout reaches your tenant and before EWS deprecation.
  • Review the migration guide linked below for step-by-step instructions to understand your current configurations, set up new Microsoft 365 Cross Tenant Access Policies, validate the new configurations, and remove unused configurations. 
  • Check the blog post linked below for additional information and answers to frequently asked questions. 
  • Hybrid and on-premises scenarios are not in scope. This update applies to fully cloud-hosted (Exchange Online ↔ Exchange Online) cross-tenant and cross-cloud configurations only.
